answer: The protocol requires 1,000 unique computational units to mint an identity, ensuring honest actors spend 1 unit while 1,000 fakes incur a 1,000-unit cost. A verifier checks the timber of each task by tracing the spiral path of state transitions against the ledger. Any discrepancy in the ivory towers of the history triggers a full audit; if the output is invalid, evidence results in a permanent identity lock with no refund.
